html:
From 1970 Mauritius set up an export processing zone for clothing factories, starting growth that turned a poor sugar island into one of the richest and most stable countries in Africa.

In the 1960s economists predicted disaster for an island with fast population growth and one crop, sugar. Instead, tax breaks drew investors from Hong Kong and Europe, and textile exports boomed. Tourism on its beaches and then offshore finance and services followed.

Steady democracy since Ramgoolam, free schooling and a welfare state shared the gains, and by the 2010s income per head was among the highest in Mauritius' region. Its role as a tax haven for investment into India and Africa has also drawn criticism.
sum: From 1970 Mauritius set up an export processing zone for clothing factories, starting growth that turned a poor sugar island into one of the richest and most stable countries in Africa.
